segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ ״הֲרֵי זוֹ תַּחַת זוֹ״, ״תְּמוּרַת זוֹ״, ״חֲלִיפַת זוֹ״ — הֲרֵי זוֹ תְּמוּרָה. ״זוֹ מְחוּלֶּלֶת עַל זוֹ״ — אֵין זוֹ תְּמוּרָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» This mishna discusses the language that serves to effect substitution. If one said: «This» non-sacred animal «is hereby in place of that» consecrated animal, or if he said: It is «the substitute of that» consecrated animal, or if one said: It is «the exchange for that» consecrated animal, «that» non-sacred animal «is a substitute.» If he said: «This» consecrated animal «is desacralized,» with its sanctity transferred «to that» non-sacred animal, «that» non-sacred animal «is not a substitute.»

segments.he: וְאִם הָיָה הֶקְדֵּשׁ בַּעַל מוּם — יוֹצֵא לְחוּלִּין, וְצָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת דָּמִים.
segments.en: «And if the consecrated» animal «was blemished,» and he said: This consecrated animal is desacralized, with its sanctity transferred to that non-sacred animal, the consecrated animal is desacralized «and assumes non-sacred» status, by Torah law. By rabbinic law, the owner «is required to conduct» an appraisal to ascertain the relative «value» of the two animals. If the consecrated animal was worth more than the non-sacred animal, he must pay the difference to the Temple treasury.

moves.summary: Blemished consecrated animal is desacralized; appraisal required

positions.claim: 'in place of', 'substitute of', 'exchange for' effect substitution; 'desacralized onto' does not
a blemished consecrated animal desacralized onto another becomes non-sacred but requires appraisal
